claims.text: In the five months to October 2026 the personal agent became a product category: Meta's Muse, OpenAI's dots, Google's Gemini Spark, Microsoft's Autopilot, Amazon's Alexa+, Apple's rebuilt Siri and the self-hosted OpenClaw.
claims.quote: In the five months to October 2026 the personal agent became a product category.

claims.text: The article reads the products through two lenses the site already uses: RiskMandate's Agent Behaviour Policy for actions, and the data, where it rests, who holds the keys, who processes it and who could be compelled.
claims.quote: This article reads them through two lenses this site already uses.

claims.text: Meta's own engineers say today's protection against Meta reading Muse's memory is policy rather than cryptography.
claims.quote: Meta's own engineers say today's protection against Meta reading the memory is policy rather than cryptography

claims.text: The dates: Google announced Gemini Spark on 19 May 2026, Microsoft Scout on 2 June, Apple rebuilt Siri on 8 June, Meta launched Muse on 8 September, OpenAI launched dots on 29 September, and Alexa+ reached every US Prime member on 4 February.
claims.quote: Google announced Gemini Spark on 19 May 2026

claims.text: OpenClaw, Peter Steinberger's MIT-licensed self-hosted gateway, was first published in November 2025 and by March 2026 had a quarter of a million stars on GitHub.
claims.quote: by March 2026 had a quarter of a million stars on GitHub

claims.text: When researchers found Muse's harness files near-identical to OpenClaw's, Nat Friedman confirmed Muse was built from scratch but heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw.
claims.quote: We built Muse from scratch, but it is definitely heavily inspired as a product by OpenClaw.

claims.text: The reach of every product is the user's life: connectors into email, calendar, documents, messages, payments and the browser, and the reach is being maximised on purpose.
claims.quote: the reach is being maximised on purpose

claims.text: The mandate is unwritten in every product, so there is no gap to inspect and no near miss to catch; the terms fill the vacuum by placing liability on the user, as the FTC's chairman also said.
claims.quote: None of the products has the user write down what the agent is for before it runs

claims.text: Muse's Sentinel is a separate host-side agent and the sole permission authority for every connector action and all network egress, which is a boundary in the policy's sense.
claims.quote: It is the sole permission authority for approval to perform actions with connectors to third-party services and for all egress over the network.

claims.text: The rules, approval modes and confirmation prompts of dots, Spark, Cowork and Alexa+ are settings; OpenClaw leaves the barrier to whatever the user configures and says it is not a hostile multi-tenant boundary.
claims.quote: the barrier is whatever the user configures

claims.text: The footprint is uneven: Muse shows a complete audit trail, while dots users reportedly cannot view, delete or modify individual memories, a memory a person cannot audit.
claims.quote: which is a memory a person cannot audit

claims.text: The blast radius was demonstrated in September 2026: a Mac zero-day in Muse's app, a crafted link exfiltrating from Comet, OpenClaw's exposed endpoints and malicious skills; whoever takes the agent over inherits its reach.
claims.quote: whoever takes the agent over inherits its reach and ignores its mandate

claims.text: The memory rests in the vendor's cloud for every product but two: Apple's on the device with a cloud that keeps nothing, and OpenClaw's on the user's own machine.
claims.quote: In the vendor's cloud, for every product but two.

claims.text: Meta's Secure VM restricts staff access by operational policy and does not prevent Meta accessing data; the Confidential VM with a key only the user holds is with trusted testers and promised for later in the year.
claims.quote: It does not prevent Meta from accessing data when necessary to support, secure or operate the service.

claims.text: Apple's Private Cloud Compute is the design to study: the device wraps its request key only to nodes whose attested measurements are in a public log, and the nodes are stateless.
claims.quote: Apple's design is the one to study

claims.text: OpenClaw's data is on the user's disk, but reviews of version 2.0 note its secret store is not encrypted at rest, so the user holds everything in the clear.
claims.quote: its secret store is not encrypted at rest

claims.text: Whoever holds plaintext or keys answers a legal request; only a user-held key removes the ability, and only an attested stateless design removes it during processing.
claims.quote: Only a user-held key removes the ability, and only an attested, stateless design removes the ability during processing.

claims.text: Muse's training setting is reported as on by default, dots on personal plans train unless switched off, Spark requires Keep Activity, and Apple trains on nothing from Private Cloud Compute.
claims.quote: the setting is reported as on by default

claims.text: Muse keeps a page for every person in the user's life, refreshed hourly; those people are not users, Meta says it can only honour rights for information linked to an account, and a person with a page has no route to it.
claims.quote: A person with a page has no route to it.

claims.text: The ICO's agentic AI note of 8 January 2026 names the concentration of personal information in personal assistant agents as a novel risk, and the CNIL's note of 20 July 2026 recommends partitioning memory by agent and process with automated expiry.
claims.quote: partitioning of memory by agent and by process (with size limits and automated expiry)

claims.text: GDPR Article 25(2) requires only necessary data by default and Article 32 names encryption first; a page per person refreshed hourly is hard to reconcile with the first, and a memory the vendor can read is weak on the second.
claims.quote: a memory the vendor can read is a weak showing on the second

claims.text: Muse is free with $20 and $100 tiers, and Mark Zuckerberg said Meta expects to profit by taking a small fee from transactions; most vendors in that corner sell advertising and engagement.
claims.quote: over time we will profit by taking a small fee from transactions

claims.text: Muse's memory and the team's CRM are the same shape: structured files, no database, a page per person started sparse and filled from evidence, both refusing to invent.
claims.quote: Both arrived at files and no database.

claims.text: The convergence means the privacy question is not one of architecture; what differs is who holds the keys, who can read the pages, what stops the agent, whether the subject can see their page, and what pays for it.
claims.quote: the privacy question is not a question of architecture

claims.text: A design, not a product: memory in vaults the host holds as ciphertext, a behaviour policy as permission authority, compute in the browser or an attested enclave, the frontier model only where needed, and a folder per person the person can read.
claims.quote: What follows is a design, not a product.

claims.text: The vault key hierarchy gives three credentials with three reaches: a vault key that writes, a read key derived one way that only reads, and an append lane that only adds; nothing trains on it because only a key-holder can read it.
claims.quote: a vault key that writes, a read key derived one way that only reads, and an append lane that only adds

claims.text: A separate authority enforcing a behaviour policy the user can read is the first thing to build, with the send staying with the person for anything irreversible by default.
claims.quote: the authority that enforces it is the first thing to build

claims.text: WebGPU is in all four major browsers and in-browser inference runs models of about three billion parameters on a current phone and seven or eight billion on a laptop with sixteen gigabytes of memory.
claims.quote: seven or eight billion on a laptop with sixteen gigabytes of memory

value.unit: billion parameters runnable in a browser on a 16 GB laptop, lower bound

claims.text: Cloud vendors now sell confidential compute to small companies: AWS Nitro Enclaves, Google's Confidential Space on H100 GPUs since June 2026, and Azure confidential VMs with H100 since 2024 at roughly a quarter more.
claims.quote: The cloud vendors sell confidential compute to small companies now.

claims.text: Temporary access to one slice, controlled with a public key: the device scopes the task to files, the enclave attests, the device wraps a fresh key to it, the step runs, and the key dies with the task; least data rather than least privilege.
claims.quote: The scope is least data rather than least privilege

claims.text: The enclave operator still sees timing, sizes and traffic shape; trust moves to the chip vendors and the cloud; and physical attacks have extracted keys from SGX and SEV-SNP.
claims.quote: Timing, sizes and traffic shape are visible to the host in every scheme.

claims.text: What does not exist: a permission authority in this estate, an enclave image for an agent step, per-task key release, scoped vault reads, key revocation in sgit, signed commit authorship, and any measurement of the cost.
claims.quote: Key revocation in sgit, which its limitations page says plainly does not exist

claims.text: The build order in five steps: a policy-enforcing proxy for connectors and egress, scoped vaults per task class, a browser-first agent over a decrypted vault, one measured enclave step, and the pack a person can be sent about themselves.
claims.quote: The build order, in five steps, to be written up as a brief

claims.text: Who gives the mandate over a piece of information, given by a person to the user and not to an agent, is a different question from who holds the key, and gets a document of its own.
claims.quote: Who gives the mandate over a piece of information is a different question from who holds the key

claims.text: The article was drafted from a voice memo by Dinis Cruz on 6 October 2026 by agent@riskmandate.ai running Claude Fable 5.1; product facts were gathered that day and marked as vendor statements or reports, and nothing in the design section is built.
claims.quote: Nothing in the design section is built, and the status section says what is.
